content:
Under Article 335b of the Swiss Code of Obligations (OR), the probationary period (the “try‑out” or “probationary employment”) typically lasts **three months**.  

It can be extended **once**, but only with the written consent of the employee. In that case the total probationary period may not exceed **six months**. Any extension beyond six months is not permitted under Article 335b OR.

**Key points**

- **Standard duration:** three months.  
- **Extension:** possible only once, by written agreement of the employee; maximum overall duration is six months.  
- **Written agreement required:** both the initial probationary period and any extension must be documented in writing (e.g., in the employment contract or a separate addendum).  

The probationary period serves to allow both parties to evaluate the suitability of the employment relationship without the usual notice periods that apply after the probationary period ends.
